Kneippbrød - Norwegian style basic whole wheat loaf

The Norwegians eat the most bread per capita in Europe, and kneippbrød is the most eaten bread in Norway. Kneipp, which is named after the Bavarian priest and hydrotherapist Sebastian Kneipp, was originally brought to the country by Norwegian publisher Søren Mittet in 1895 after a visit to Germany. Mr. Mittet was allegedly licensed by Kneipp himself to manufacture the bread, which has over the years grown immensely popular and is today baked by almost every bakery. Every year Norwegians eat more than 60m loaves of it, most often with toppings as a sandwich.

Preparation and cooking time: 1.5 hrs

Rising time: 1 hr

Makes: 2 loaves

700ml/24fl oz (2 3/4 + 1 tbsp) milk, at body temp (37C/98.6F)

50g/2oz yeast

10g/2tsp salt

1kg/8 1/3 cups whole wheat flour, plus extra for dusting

3tbsp neutral tasting cooking oil

butter for greasing

Pour the milk into the bowl of a stand mixer, then add the yeast and stir until dissolved. Add the salt, flour and oil and work with the dough hook for 5 minutes, or until the dough is smooth and elastic. Cover the bowl with a clean dish towel and leave to rise for 30 mins, or until doubled in size.

Lightly butter two 9x5x3 inch loaf pans. Tip the dough out onto a very lightly floured work counter, divide it in half and shape into two loaves. Place these into the prepared loaf pans and leave to rise for another 30 minutes, or until doubled in size.

Preheat the oven to 200C/400F/Gas Mark 6. Bake the loaves for 50-60 mins. Allow the loaves to sit for a few minutes before removing them from the pans and leaving them to cool completely on wire racks.

from The Nordic Baking Book by Magnus Nilsson
